title: Copenhagen Business School Summer University
description: One of Europe's longest-running summer university programs (est. 1999), offering roughly 50 business and interdisciplinary bachelor/master-level courses in 2-, 3-, or 6-week formats at CBS's Copenhagen campus each summer; about 2,000-2,500 students from 50+ countries attend annually. Access is category-based rather than a single competitive application: CBS students, university-nominated exchange/AURORA students, and Danish credit-transfer students pay no tuition, while 'Single Course' (EU/EEA/Swiss citizens) and 'Freemover' (non-EU) applicants who have completed upper secondary (high school) education can enroll by paying per-course tuition -- making the entry-level categories realistic mainly for a student who has already finished secondary school, not a current 14-18-year-old.
citizenship_restrictions: None for exchange/AURORA/credit-transfer categories with home-institution nomination; the 'Single Course' category requires EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship or Danish permanent residence; non-EU/EEA applicants instead apply as fee-paying 'Freemovers'.
application_requirements: completed upper secondary (high school) exam, for Single Course/Freemover categories
category-appropriate online application (MoveOn or CBS portal)
per-course tuition payment for non-nominated categories (6,150-15,000 DKK depending on category)
selectivity_evidence: CBS's own eligibility page defines entry by category (nomination, citizenship/residency, or having completed high school) rather than by competitive review; no GPA cutoff, essay, or acceptance-rate language appears on the official pages.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle (first round closed 2026-04-14; second round, 2-week courses only, closed 2026-05-05; courses ran through 2026-07-31)
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: AI Summer Week @ ETH Zurich
organization: ETH Zurich, Department of Computer Science (D-INFK), in partnership with Hebbian
description: A five-day, in-person program for students aged 13-18 held at ETH Zurich's Department of Computer Science, run jointly by D-INFK and Hebbian (a Zurich-based youth STEM workshop provider founded by an ETH alumnus and an ETH doctoral student). Participants use AI tools (ChatGPT, Playground AI, Lovable, Shopify) to design, build, and market their own online product/business, culminating in a pitch to a judging panel that has included representatives from Google, Apple, and ETH Zurich. ETH's own department page frames it as becoming 'a regular feature' of its outreach activities; the 2025 pilot had 19 participants. This is the only current ETH Zurich summer offering confirmed open to high-school-aged students -- ETH's general summer-schools landing page (ethz.ch) explicitly limits its other listed summer schools to Bachelor's, Master's, and doctoral students.
application_requirements: online application form (personal/school details, date of birth, contact info)
CHF 500 program fee (need-based scholarship assistance available)
selectivity_evidence: Application requires a motivation statement and optional CV/LinkedIn; the 2025 cohort was capped at 19 students, but neither ETH's nor Hebbian's pages state an acceptance rate or explicit selection criteria beyond the application form.
current_cycle_label: 2026 (Aug 3-7, 2026; application deadline June 15, 2026 already passed at time of research)
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Koç University Summer Academy (High School Programs)
description: Koç University's on-campus, non-residential (day) summer program in Istanbul for high school students who have completed prep-year, 9th, 10th, or 11th grade. Courses (Law, Introduction to Programming with Python, Experimental Physics, Psychology, Applied Molecular Biology and Genetics, Nanotechnology, and Economics) are adapted from KU's undergraduate curriculum and taught face-to-face by KU faculty, research assistants, and student mentors, alongside a 'Meeting Hour with Academics', sports sessions, and campus activities. English-taught courses require CEFR B2+ proficiency. 2026 session: June 29-July 10, 2026 (Mon-Thu classes, Friday activities); fee TRY 80,000 covering education, materials, and activities, with a shuttle available for an extra fee (no on-campus accommodation).
application_requirements: completed prep/9th/10th/11th grade at time of application
CEFR B2 or above English proficiency for English-taught courses
selectivity_evidence: The official pages describe eligibility (grade level, language proficiency) and a fee-payment process, with no GPA cutoff, essay, or stated acceptance rate -- enrollment appears bounded by eligibility and available seats rather than competitive review.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Bilkent University Summer Camp (Yaz Kampı)
description: A two-week, faculty-taught summer camp on Bilkent University's Ankara campus for students who will have completed 9th-12th grade by June 2026. Students select courses (grouped by color-coded subject tracks, one course per group) taught by Bilkent faculty, plus cultural/social/sporting activities; optional 2-person-room dormitory stay is available. 2026 session: July 13-24, 2026 (campus/dorm access from July 12); fee TRY 68,000 with accommodation or TRY 61,000 without (both include tuition, activities, and lunch), with a 10% sibling discount. No scholarships are offered. Instruction is in Turkish and/or English depending on the course. Registration for the 2026 cycle is confirmed closed as of this research ('Kayıtlarımız kapandı' -- 'Our registrations are closed').
selectivity_evidence: The official FAQ page states eligibility purely in terms of completed grade level and required documents; there is no mention of an admissions review, GPA threshold, or acceptance rate.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Boğaziçi University BOUN101 High School Summer School (Lise Yaz Okulu)
description: A Turkish-language, non-residential summer program for high school students ('BOUN101 Lise Yaz Okulu') run by Boğaziçi University's continuing-education arm, BÜYEM, at the university's South Campus in Bebek, Istanbul. In recent cycles students selected a set of courses from a wider catalog; BÜYEM also runs a parallel BOUN101 winter edition. BÜYEM's own announcements feed confirms the 2026 cohort's certificate ceremony was completed by August 3, 2026. At the time of this research, the program's course-specific listing pages (buyem.bogazici.edu.tr/course/boun101-lise-yaz-okulu/...) had already been taken down following the program's completion, and the dedicated boun101.boun.edu.tr subdomain could not be reached, so this year's exact fee, course list, and precise date range could not be independently re-confirmed beyond BÜYEM's own program-completion announcement -- those fields are intentionally left blank rather than carried over from stale prior-year listings.
application_requirements: online registration via BÜYEM (specific requirements for the 2026 course listing were no longer accessible at time of research)
selectivity_evidence: Not directly confirmed -- the course-specific admissions/eligibility page could not be reached during this research; BÜYEM's other continuing-education programs are generally fee-based enrollment rather than competitive admission.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cohort completed (certificate ceremony by 2026-08-03 per BÜYEM's own announcement); 2027 cycle not yet published

title: ODTÜ (METU) Engineering Summer School (Mühendislik Yaz Okulu)
organization: Middle East Technical University (ODTÜ); organized by Arber Kongre A.Ş. with METU faculty (2026 edition to be organized by Radyo ODTÜ)
description: A two-week, in-person engineering exposure program for 10th-12th grade high schoolers on METU's Ankara campus, coordinated by METU Metallurgical & Materials Engineering professor Y. Eren Kalay (with administrative organization historically by Arber Kongre A.Ş.), covering aerospace/aerodynamics, nanotechnology, MEMS/electronics, robotics & AI, bio-inspired design, and non-destructive testing through METU faculty-led lectures and lab work at METU's own research centers (RÜZGEM, MEMS, ROMER, KATAMER, etc.), plus site visits to TUSAŞ and ASELSAN. Taught in Turkish (no English requirement); capped at 90 students; historical fee TRY 60,000 with early-bird/ODTÜ-affiliation discounts, no need-based financial aid found. Important caveat: the organizer's own site, at the time of this research, still displays the 2025 session's dates (June 30 - July 11, 2025) and carries a banner stating 'ODTÜ Mühendislik Yaz Okulu 2026'da Radyo ODTÜ tarafından düzenlenecektir' (the 2026 edition will instead be organized by Radyo ODTÜ, a METU student radio society) -- no 2026 dates, fees, or application process have been published on this domain as of retrieval, so 2026-specific date/cost fields below are left blank rather than carried over from the stale 2025 listing.
application_requirements: payment within 2 weeks of acceptance to finalize enrollment (registrations confirmed in payment order given a 90-student cap)
selectivity_evidence: Enrollment is described as a 3-step eligibility-check-then-payment process, with spots 'confirmed in order of payment' up to a 90-student cap -- effectively first-come-first-served among eligible applicants rather than merit-based competitive admission.
current_cycle_label: 2025 cycle shown on organizer's site (stale); 2026 edition announced to be organized separately by Radyo ODTÜ with no dates yet published
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: UWC Short Courses
description: A worldwide directory of UWC-endorsed short courses (roughly 1-5 weeks each, in-person, online, or hybrid), covering themes such as peace/conflict resolution, leadership for global impact, social entrepreneurship and innovation, environmental sustainability, and identity/diversity/inclusion. Per UWC's own 'Apply for a short course' page, most courses are for young people aged 13-20 (some are designed for adults, or even younger participants), run mostly June-August (though the live directory also lists courses spanning the full year), charge a fee covering tuition/accommodation/meals/activities with need-based financial support available, and each individual course sets its own eligibility, timeline, and application process rather than there being one unified UWC Short Courses deadline or cost. As of this research, the live directory listed dozens of specific named 2026 courses (in-person courses in Spain, Vietnam, Armenia, Netherlands, Tanzania, Belgium, Brazil, China, the UK, and Germany, plus numerous online courses) with several still accepting applications for sessions running into September-December 2026.
citizenship_restrictions: Varies by individual course; UWC states most courses welcome all nationalities, with some carrying a regional focus or language requirement.
application_requirements: varies by individual course -- typically an online application via the course's own listing page
selectivity_evidence: UWC states 'places are limited' across short courses generally, but selection criteria, essays, or acceptance rates are set individually per course rather than centrally, so no single selectivity level applies to 'UWC Short Courses' as a whole.
current_cycle_label: Rolling 2026 directory -- dozens of individual courses live as of 2026-08-20, several still open for sessions through December 2026
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
